messages.content: How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?

function.name: calculate_vector_angle
function.description: Calculate the angle of a vector based on its X and Y components. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

X_component.description: The X component of the vector. This is a float type value.

Y_component.description: The Y component of the vector. This is a float type value.

use_degrees.description: If true, the result will be in degrees. If false, the result will be in radians. Default is false.

message.content:
Sure! To determine the angle of a vector (like a force or momentum vector) relative to the horizontal axis, you need its X and Y components. Once you have those, you can use the arctangent function (often called `atan2`) to get the angle.

If you already know the X and Y components of the momentum (or force) vector, just let me know them and I can calculate the angle for you. If you’re looking for a general explanation or formula, here it is:

\[
\theta = \operatorname{atan2}(Y_{\text{component}}, X_{\text{component}})
\]

This gives the angle in radians. If you prefer degrees, you can convert it by multiplying by \(180/\pi\).

Let me know the components, and I’ll compute the angle for you!
